title: 1998 AHSME Problem 14
statement: A parabola has vertex at \((4,-5)\) and has two \(x\)-intercepts, one positive and one negative. If this parabola is the graph of \(y=ax^2+bx+c,\) which of \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) must be positive?

solutions.text: The parabola opens upward, so \(a\gt0.\) Its roots have opposite signs, so \(\frac{c}{a}\lt0\) and hence \(c\lt0.\) Also \(-\frac{b}{2a}=4\gt0,\) so \(b\lt0.\) Therefore only \(a\) must be positive, and A is correct.
hints: The vertex lies below two intercepts, so determine the opening direction
Use the signs of the roots’ product and of \(-\frac{b}{2a}=4\)
